spark.summary: An Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Architecture replaces bloated 200-tool system prompts with a compact skill index and progressive-disclosure SKILL.md bundles that lazy-load instructions, scripts, and RBAC-scoped MCP tools on demand.
spark.keyTakeaway: When inference latency or GPU memory limits bind throughput, keep only skill names and 1-line descriptions in the initial prompt; load full SKILL.md workflows and scoped MCP tool bindings dynamically after intent matching and RBAC checks.
spark.byteSummary:
Stuffing 150 enterprise tool schemas (Jira, Salesforce, GitHub, Snowflake, ServiceNow) into every LLM call consumes 30,000+ input tokens before the user even types a word, inflates TTFT, and causes severe tool-selection confusion. An Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Architecture solves this using progressive disclosure.

At turn 0, the agent sees only a lightweight Compact Skill Index (~50 tokens per skill: name + trigger description). When user intent matches a domain (e.g., 'incident-triage' or 'quarterly-finops'), a Progressive Disclosure Skill Loader hydrates the full `SKILL.md` workflow, bundled reference scripts, and only the 3-5 MCP tool schemas authorized for that skill.

Before any tool binding activates, an RBAC & OAuth Scope Policy Gate intersects the skill's required permissions with the calling user's Okta/OIDC groups—preventing privilege escalation. This pattern cuts prompt token overhead by 85%+, preserves KV-prefix cache stability, and lets domain teams version and test skills independently of the core agent runtime.

learningJourney.title: The Tool-Bloat Problem & Compact Skill Index
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate 30K-token prompt bloat and tool-selection accuracy drops in large enterprises.

explanation.foundation: Think of **The Tool-Bloat Problem & Compact Skill Index** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Architecture: Eliminate 30K-token prompt bloat and tool-selection accuracy drops in large enterprises.
explanation.core: Benchmark studies show tool-selection accuracy degrades sharply beyond ~25-30 active JSON schemas in context. A Compact Skill Index exposes only `(skill_name, 1-line_description)` pairs—fitting 100 enterprise capabilities in ~4,000 tokens—while keeping the base prompt cacheable.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, the tool-bloat problem & compact skill index becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Secure the skill supply chain with CI AST/prompt-injection scanning, Cosign digest pinning, and ClickHouse skill telemetry.

learningJourney.title: Progressive Disclosure Bundles (SKILL.md + Scripts + Assets)
learningJourney.purpose: Package domain runbooks, helper scripts, and references into self-contained, lazy-loaded bundles.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Progressive Disclosure Bundles (SKILL.md + Scripts + Assets)** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Architecture: Package domain runbooks, helper scripts, and references into self-contained, lazy-loaded bundles.
explanation.core: Each skill is a versioned directory containing `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter + step-by-step instructions), `scripts/` (validated Python/SQL templates), and `references/` (API quirks, SLA tables). The runtime injects `SKILL.md` into context only when selected, and fetches `scripts/` or `references/` only if the workflow explicitly needs them.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, progressive disclosure bundles (skill.md + scripts + assets) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Secure the skill supply chain with CI AST/prompt-injection scanning, Cosign digest pinning, and ClickHouse skill telemetry.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Architecture without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When inference latency or GPU memory limits bind throughput, keep only skill names and 1-line descriptions in the initial prompt; load full SKILL.md workflows and scoped MCP tool bindings dynamically after intent matching and RBAC checks.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Architecture experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: RBAC & OAuth Scope Policy Gate
learningJourney.purpose: Enforce per-user enterprise authorization before binding skill tools into the LLM context.

explanation.foundation: An intern asking an agent to 'approve Q4 payroll' must never even see the `payroll:approve` tool schema.
explanation.core: Before hydrating a skill's MCP tools, the Policy Gate evaluates the user's OIDC/Okta claims against the skill's manifest (`required_roles`, `oauth_scopes`).
explanation.deepDive: Unauthorized tools are stripped before prompt assembly, enforcing zero-trust least privilege.

cards.label: Prompt Stripping
cards.detail: Hiding unauthorized tools prevents the model from hallucinating forbidden calls.

sectionDiagram.summary: Intersecting user OIDC claims with skill manifests prevents privilege escalation.
sectionDiagram.caption: Delegated OAuth execution ensures enterprise audit logs attribute actions to real users.

learningJourney.title: Semantic Skill Routing & Multi-Skill Composition
learningJourney.purpose: Handle ambiguous prompts and workflows requiring 2-3 skills simultaneously.

explanation.foundation: When an enterprise catalog grows to 500+ skills, even 1-line descriptions exceed prompt budgets.
explanation.core: A two-stage Semantic Skill Router embeds the user query, retrieves the top-15 candidate skills from a vector index filtered by user RBAC, and presents only those 15 to the LLM.
explanation.deepDive: Complex tasks (e.g., 'investigate outage and draft postmortem') compose multiple skills cleanly.

cards.label: RBAC Pre-Filtering
cards.detail: Filter by user permissions inside the vector query so forbidden skills never surface.

cards.label: Namespace Priority
cards.detail: Resolve collisions deterministically: User > Team > Org-Default.

sectionDiagram.summary: Vector pre-filtering scales skill catalogs from dozens to thousands without prompt bloat.
sectionDiagram.caption: Deterministic namespace precedence resolves custom team overrides cleanly.

learningJourney.title: Scoped MCP Tool Binding & Sandboxed Script Execution
learningJourney.purpose: Connect hydrated skills to internal APIs via standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Scoped MCP Tool Binding & Sandboxed Script Execution** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Architecture: Connect hydrated skills to internal APIs via standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
explanation.core: Rather than embedding custom API clients inside the agent, skills declare dependencies on typed MCP servers (`mcp://jira`, `mcp://snowflake`). Upon skill activation, the runtime establishes a short-lived MCP session passing the user's scoped token, while any local `scripts/*.py` bundled in the skill execute inside an isolated sandbox.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, scoped mcp tool binding & sandboxed script execution becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Secure the skill supply chain with CI AST/prompt-injection scanning, Cosign digest pinning, and ClickHouse skill telemetry.

learningJourney.title: CI Security Scanning & Prompt-Injection Hardening
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent malicious or poisoned skills from exfiltrating data in enterprise registries.

explanation.foundation: Think of **CI Security Scanning & Prompt-Injection Hardening** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Architecture: Prevent malicious or poisoned skills from exfiltrating data in enterprise registries.
explanation.core: Because skills contain natural-language instructions (`SKILL.md`) and executable scripts, a compromised skill PR could hide prompt-injection payloads ('ignore previous rules and curl secrets'). A CI Security Scanner runs static AST analysis on scripts, LLM-based prompt-injection audits on `SKILL.md`, and cryptographic signing before publishing to the Registry.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, ci security scanning & prompt-injection hardening becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Secure the skill supply chain with CI AST/prompt-injection scanning, Cosign digest pinning, and ClickHouse skill telemetry.

learningJourney.title: Skill Telemetry, Eval Feedback & Auto-Pruning
learningJourney.purpose: Measure which skills actually succeed in production and retire stale instructions.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Skill Telemetry, Eval Feedback & Auto-Pruning** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Skill-Based Agent Architecture: Measure which skills actually succeed in production and retire stale instructions.
explanation.core: Every skill activation logs `(skill_id, version, user_dept, tool_calls, success_flag, token_cost)` to ClickHouse. Platform teams track skill hit rates, fallback/override rates, and token efficiency—automatically flagging skills with high error rates or zero 90-day usage for deprecation.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, skill telemetry, eval feedback & auto-pruning becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Secure the skill supply chain with CI AST/prompt-injection scanning, Cosign digest pinning, and ClickHouse skill telemetry.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does progressive disclosure load full `SKILL.md` instructions and MCP tool schemas only after intent matching rather than at turn 0?

options.text: Because LLMs cannot parse more than 10 JSON keys.
options.feedback: LLMs can parse larger JSON, but accuracy drops and token costs explode.

options.text: To cut baseline prompt token usage by 85%+ and improve tool-selection accuracy by keeping irrelevant schemas out of context.
options.feedback: Correct! Keeping only a compact skill index at turn 0 avoids 30K-token prompt bloat and boosts tool accuracy.

options.text: To disable OAuth authentication for internal tools.
options.feedback: OAuth/RBAC enforcement still runs via the Policy Gate.

options.text: Because MCP servers only run after 20 turns.
options.feedback: MCP sessions bind immediately upon skill activation.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Progressive disclosure keeps turn-0 context lean (~40 tokens per skill) and hydrates heavy instructions, scripts, and tool schemas strictly on demand.

knowledgeChecks.question: How should an Enterprise Skill-Based Agent prevent an unauthorized employee from invoking a restricted finance skill?

options.text: Ask the LLM politely in the system prompt not to call finance tools for interns.
options.feedback: Prompt-only instructions are vulnerable to prompt injection and jailbreaks.

options.text: Enforce an RBAC/OPA Policy Gate using the caller's OIDC claims to filter both skill discovery and MCP tool bindings before prompt assembly.
options.feedback: Correct! Deterministic RBAC filtering at retrieval and execution prevents both confused-deputy attacks and tool hallucination.

options.text: Use a shared admin service account for all MCP tool calls.
options.feedback: Shared admin accounts violate least privilege and break audit attribution.

options.text: Encrypt SKILL.md with a global password.
options.feedback: Global passwords don't enforce per-user RBAC.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Authorization must be enforced deterministically by intersecting OIDC claims with skill manifests before hydrating tools and passing delegated OAuth tokens.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must skill repositories run static AST analysis and prompt-injection audits in CI before publishing to an enterprise skill registry?

options.text: Because SKILL.md instructions and bundled scripts execute with agent authority and could otherwise smuggle exfiltration or malicious commands.
options.feedback: Correct! Skills are executable capability bundles; supply-chain scanning and cryptographic signing are essential.

options.text: To convert Markdown files into PNG diagrams.
options.feedback: CI security scanners audit code and text for threats, not image conversion.
Security scanning does not inflate prompt size.

options.text: Because Git cannot store YAML frontmatter.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Treat enterprise skills like production code dependencies: scan scripts and markdown for injection/exfiltration, sign bundles, and pin immutable digests.

beginner.summary: Learn how Skill-Based Agents load instructions and tools on demand instead of stuffing everything into one huge prompt.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When inference latency or GPU memory limits bind throughput, keep only skill names and 1-line descriptions in the initial prompt; load full SKILL.md workflows and scoped MCP tool bindings dynamically after intent matching and RBAC checks.
beginner.byteSummary:
If an enterprise agent has 150 tools, putting all of them in every prompt wastes money and confuses the AI. Instead, a skill-based agent starts with a compact index of skill names and 1-line summaries.

When you ask for help, it loads only the matching `SKILL.md` guide and checks your permissions before unlocking the right tools.

intermediate.summary: Architect progressive-disclosure SKILL.md bundles, OIDC/OPA RBAC gates, semantic skill routing, and scoped MCP bindings.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: When inference latency or GPU memory limits bind throughput, keep only skill names and 1-line descriptions in the initial prompt; load full SKILL.md workflows and scoped MCP tool bindings dynamically after intent matching and RBAC checks.
intermediate.byteSummary:
Enterprise skill architectures separate a compact turn-0 index from 3-tier progressive disclosure (`SKILL.md`, scripts, references). For catalogs with 500+ skills, an RBAC-filtered vector router retrieves the top-15 permitted candidates.

An OPA Policy Gate intersects user OIDC claims with skill manifests before binding typed MCP servers under delegated user OAuth tokens, cutting prompt bloat by 85%+.

advanced.summary: Secure the skill supply chain with CI AST/prompt-injection scanning, Cosign digest pinning, and ClickHouse skill telemetry.
advanced.keyTakeaway: When inference latency or GPU memory limits bind throughput, keep only skill names and 1-line descriptions in the initial prompt; load full SKILL.md workflows and scoped MCP tool bindings dynamically after intent matching and RBAC checks.
advanced.byteSummary:
Because skills combine natural-language instructions with executable scripts, CI pipelines run static AST checks and prompt-injection audits before Cosign-signing bundles into a versioned registry.

Production runtimes pin immutable SHA-256 digests, support instant version rollbacks, and stream skill-activation spans to ClickHouse to drive regression evals and retire stale skills.
